haiku-low.q1: They look the same: both return the same 401 and "Invalid email or password" page. A dummy bcrypt compare equalizes timing, so the response does not reveal which accounts exist.
haiku-low.q2: It returns 429 immediately with Retry-After and "Too many attempts. Try again later." The password is not checked and nothing is recorded.
haiku-low.q3: Only on a successful login is it replaced: the old session is deleted in the same transaction as the new one. A failed login leaves the existing session untouched.
haiku-low.q4: Only an opaque random session ID, base64url-encoded, with HttpOnly, Secure and SameSite=Lax. HttpOnly means page scripts cannot read it.
haiku-low.q5: After 12 hours from creation, even with constant activity. Activity resets the 30-minute idle clock but never extends the 12-hour absolute cap.
haiku-low.q6: It redirects to /login, clears the cookie with Max-Age=0, and deletes the session row if one exists.
haiku-low.q7: The server deletes the session row before replying. If no cookie or the row is already gone, it still redirects to /login and clears the cookie.
haiku-low.q8: In the shared Postgres database. Any instance hashes the cookie ID with sha256 and looks up the matching row in the sessions table.
haiku-low.q9: In the login_failures table, keyed by trimmed lowercased email with attempted_at. The server counts rows where attempted_at is within the last 10 minutes, using the database clock.
haiku-low.q10: It compares last_seen_at to now() minus 30 minutes and created_at to now() minus 12 hours. If valid, it writes last_seen_at = now().
haiku-low.q11: HTTP 503 with "Sign-in is temporarily unavailable. Please try again in a moment." No session is issued and the password is not accepted.
haiku-low.q12: A sweeper every 5 minutes, run by whichever instance gets the advisory lock, deletes sessions idle over 30 minutes or older than 12 hours. Expired requests also delete their own row.

sonnet.q1: It doesn't differ. Unknown email and wrong password share one code path, the same 401 and the same login page ("Invalid email or password"). A dummy bcrypt compare makes the timing match, and the failure is recorded the same way.
sonnet.q2: The email is locked out (locked_until > now()). The server returns 429 immediately with a Retry-After header and the "Too many attempts. Try again later." page. It does not check the password and records nothing.
sonnet.q3: On a successful login, the old cookie's session row is deleted in the same transaction that inserts the new session. A new random ID is always generated. If the login fails (401, 429 or 503), the existing session is left untouched.
sonnet.q4: Only an opaque random session ID (sid=<id>), with no user data. It is HttpOnly, so page scripts cannot read it. It is also Secure and SameSite=Lax.
sonnet.q5: At 12 hours after the session's created_at. Activity restarts the 30-minute idle clock but never extends the 12-hour cap, because created_at is never updated.
sonnet.q6: The server deletes that session's row if one exists, then redirects (302) to /login and clears the cookie with a Set-Cookie. Missing, unknown and expired sessions are all handled the same way.
sonnet.q7: The server deletes the session row by id_hash before replying, then returns 302 to /login and clears the cookie. If the session is already gone (0 rows deleted) or there is no cookie, that is fine and it replies the same way. If the delete hits a storage error, it returns 503 and keeps the cookie.
sonnet.q8: Session state is kept in the shared Postgres sessions table. Either instance hashes the cookie's ID with sha256 and looks up id_hash in that table, so no sticky sessions are needed.
sonnet.q9: In the Postgres login_failures table, with rows of (email, attempted_at). The email is the trimmed, lowercased text the user typed. The window is a sliding one: the server counts rows with attempted_at > now() - 10 minutes, using the database clock.
sonnet.q10: One atomic UPDATE compares last_seen_at against now() - 30 minutes (idle) and created_at against now() - 12 hours (age), using the database clock, matching on id_hash. If it matches, it writes last_seen_at = now() and returns user_id.
sonnet.q11: HTTP 503 with a login page saying "Sign-in is temporarily unavailable. Please try again in a moment." No session is issued and no session cookie is set. The password is not accepted.
sonnet.q12: Two things. Lazy cleanup deletes a session's own row when a request using it is rejected as expired. The sweeper runs every 5 minutes on whichever instance wins pg_try_advisory_lock. It deletes sessions idle over 30 minutes or older than 12 hours. For users who never come back, the sweeper is the one that removes the rows.
